I am an old woman, 72 years, farming my small piece of land here in Mtwara. I grow my nuts the way my people have always grown them — no money for these fertilizers from the shop, and the cashew and groundnut do not need them like maize does. I will put some manure from the goats when I can, use the seeds I saved from last season, and my children and grandchildren will help me with the weeding and harvest. The rains come from God, I cannot water this land myself.
